newsitem.title: CONGO: U.S. says scaling down Zaire evacuation watch.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says scaling down Zaire evacuation watch.

text.p: The United States, one of five Western nations with troops on standby in Congo to evacuate foreigners from Zaire, said on Sunday that it was scaling down its operation as peace returned to the capital Kinshasa.

Commander Bob Anderson, spokesman for the U.S. troops deployed for Operation Guardian Retrieval, told Reuters that Marine forward units in Brazzaville would return to the USS Kearsarge amphibious assault vessel in the Atlantic off Zaire.
But he said the Kearsarge would remain off-shore until further notice should they still need to respond to protect American nationals and the embassy.

"The situation doesn't warrant keeping these extra guys forward. The situation has gone quiet over there," he said, referring to developments across the Zaire River in Kinshasa where Laurent Kabila's rebels were consolidating their hold.
"We are still in a position where we can be in Kinshasa in a matter of hours," he added.
Anderson said about 150 members of the U.S. contingent would remain at Brazzaville's Maya-Maya international airport to deal with command and control operations.
France, Belgium, Britain and Portugal also have troops in Congo.
